title: A Semantic Framework for Modelling Quotes in Email Conversations
research_question: How can email quotes and their responses be represented in a lightweight semantic model and extracted from mailing-list archives to support finer-grained queries and interaction analysis?
methodology: Manual reply-style survey of public W3C LOD and Media Fragments messages; SIOC Quotes ontology design with OWL2-RL property chains; Python regular-expression extraction from an OWL-WG mbox archive; SPARQL retrieval and weighted author-network demonstrations. Sources: R04-F01–R04-F07; exact populations and numeric settings are in topic02.metrics.

key_findings.evidence_note: Descriptive empirical counts; Table 1 has an unresolved count/percentage discrepancy and a conditional category-total conflict recorded as R04-I01.

limitations: No Topic labels, segmentation benchmark, extraction precision/recall, IAA, or evidence-preservation evaluation is reported (Sections 2.2 and 4).
Direct email domain is restricted to public technical mailing lists; business-email transfer is untested.

R04-I01/I02 preserve source count/percentage conflicts; the category-total conflict is conditional on an exclusive partition. R04-I03/I04 retain printed property-name mismatches, not a tested failure of the external ontology.
Several-parts and non-disjoint-class capabilities describe the ontology, not measured gold/model Topic overlap (R04-F03).
Author attribution assumes the author of the replied-to item authored the quote; copied/nested cases lack validation (R04-F04, R04-INT02).
No ablation, independent baseline, held-out evaluation, or repeated runtime study is reported; social-network utility is qualitative (R04-F05/F07).

paper_tasks: Rule-based inline quote/response extraction with processing counts and elapsed time

annotation_unit.value: Whole email for manual reply-style classification; no Topic span annotations. Quote/Response/Block are representation units, not an annotated span gold standard.

prediction_unit.value: Regex-extracted quoted text and response content grouped into RDF blocks; original email metadata. No Topic label or exact source-offset output is specified.

contiguity.value: Sub-message quote/response structures plus cross-message reply links. No exhaustive contiguous Topic partition or non-sequential Topic clustering algorithm. Several quoted parts may link to one overall response, but explicit offset lists/order constraints are not specified.

label_cardinality.gold: Reply-style classification is presented as message categories. If the categories are intended as an exclusive partition, their totals conflict (R04-I01). The paper does not supply a protocol that resolves this; overlapping survey labels are not inferred. No gold Topic labels or Topic membership counts.
label_cardinality.prediction: No predicted Topic memberships. Multiple blocks per email are possible, but extractor multiplicity constraints are not reported.
label_cardinality.representation: No ontology cardinality restrictions on Block/Quote/Response relations; this is not evidence of multiple Topics per span.

prediction.within_one_message: No measured discontinuous Topic output; separate quote parts are representable within one block, but extractor success on that case is unreported.
prediction.thread_level: Quote–response reply relations connect messages; they do not establish identity of a concrete work matter.

discontinuity.representation: Several quote parts before one overall response are explicitly allowed. A Block becoming a Quote later is thread-level role reuse, not demonstrated within-message discontinuous Topic assignment.

overlap.prediction: Unsupported/unreported for overlapping span assignments or multiple Topic memberships.
overlap.scope: Absence of class disjointness permits one object to be Block and Quote across conversational reuse. Ontology class overlap and unrestricted object links must not be equated with overlapping character spans or Topic labels.

dataset_domain.transfer_limit: Direct email evidence, but not private business email, Outlook HTML, Teams, attachments, or multilingual evaluation.

annotation_process.value: Authors manually analyzed reply structure using the stated categories. Annotator count, instructions beyond category definitions, adjudication, span alignment, and released annotation records are not reported.

material_inconsistencies.kind: Printed count/percentage conflict and conditional category-total conflict; visually confirmed in PDF page 2 at xhigh
material_inconsistencies.reported_values: LOD: Replies 449; top 162; inline 287; w/o message 15 (00.33%). MF: Replies 200; top 55; inline 145; w/o message 7 (00.35%). Prose says w/o-message replies less than 0.5%.
material_inconsistencies.analyst_arithmetic: 15/449 = 3.3408%; 7/200 = 3.5%. Even all-message denominators give 15/554 = 2.7076% and 7/275 = 2.5455%. Top + inline already equals total replies (449 and 200); adding w/o-message gives 464 and 207. If the listed reply styles are intended as an exclusive partition, their category totals conflict with the reported reply totals. The count/percentage conflict remains under either stated denominator.
material_inconsistencies.resolution: Retain every printed value and the prose claim. The intended correction and annotation counting protocol are not recoverable from this source. Do not change any count or infer overlapping survey labels. This is a documented source inconsistency, not a remaining contradiction in the analysis.

material_inconsistencies.kind: Material count/percentage conflict; visually confirmed in PDF page 2
material_inconsistencies.reported_values: MF most active participant: 71 posts out of 275, hence 27%.
material_inconsistencies.resolution: Retain both the reported 71/275 counts and 27%. The count-derived 25.8182% is analyst arithmetic, not a replacement source result. The intended correction is not reported; ordinary whole-percent rounding does not yield 27%.

material_inconsistencies.kind: Property namespace inconsistency; visually confirmed in PDF page 3
material_inconsistencies.reported_values: Figure 3 prints sioc:has_block :block, whereas Section 3.1 and Figure 2 define quotes:has_block.
material_inconsistencies.resolution: Retain the printed namespace mismatch. Section 3.1, Figure 2, and Figure 6 use quotes:has_block, but the intended correction to Figure 3 is not established by the paper. The external ontology was not fetched or tested, and no implementation failure is claimed.

material_inconsistencies.kind: Property-name inconsistency; visually confirmed in PDF pages 4–5
material_inconsistencies.reported_values: Section 3.2.2 calls block containment has_reply, then uses has_response; Section 3.1 and Figure 6 use quotes:has_response.
material_inconsistencies.resolution: Retain the printed naming discrepancy. Block containment is described as has_reply and then has_response in Section 3.2.2; Figure 6 separately uses quotes:has_response in the chain whose inferred relation is sioc:has_reply. These roles are distinct. The intended prose correction and external ontology behavior are not established.

material_inconsistencies.kind: Source wording mismatch; likely terminology typo by contextual interpretation, not confirmed author intent; visually confirmed in PDF page 5
material_inconsistencies.reported_values: Section 4.1 prints inline queries while describing quote extraction and counting inline replies.
material_inconsistencies.resolution: Preserve inline queries in quotations. The section title, extraction method, and inline-reply counts support reading the task as quote extraction. Calling the wording a typo is an analyst interpretation. No question-extraction evaluation or further material contradiction is inferred.
material_inconsistencies.materiality: Nonmaterial to task identification after full-context verification; retained under its existing ID for audit continuity.

rq_relevance.RQ1: R04-F02 supplies a structural quote–response unit; no comparison with sentence, clause, span, EDU, or hybrid units.
rq_relevance.RQ2: R04-F03/F04 motivate finer email relations; no Topic clusters or interleaving Topic evaluation.
rq_relevance.RQ3: R04-F03 allows several quote parts and non-disjoint classes; no Topic gold/model cardinality or span overlap.
rq_relevance.RQ4: Direct email representation support for several quoted parts per block; no direct discontinuous/overlapping Topic extraction result.
rq_relevance.RQ5: R04-F04/F06 are relevant to attribution and reply scope, but no semantic preservation measurements.
rq_relevance.RQ6: R04-F01/F05/F06 report descriptive counts/runtime/query matches. R04-I01/I02 prevent unqualified use of some percentages.
rq_relevance.RQ7: Manual survey and archive domain specified; IAA, held-out splits, duplicate controls, and Topic labels absent.
rq_relevance.RQ8: Supports investigating quote–response links as optional evidence; experiments below are untested and do not approve architecture.

interpretation.text: A quote–response link can preserve a narrower reply target than whole-message membership. It remains evidence about discourse, not proof that a block or thread equals a Topic.

The author-inference rule can misattribute copied or nested quotations if the replied-to message author did not author every quoted passage. This is a plausible failure mechanism, not an error measured by R04.

source.section: Section 2.1 reports multi-email copying not observed in the examined emails

interpretation.text: A literal +1 match can retrieve explicit support while failing to resolve which proposition, exception, or condition is endorsed. R04 does not test these semantic cases or prove full evidence preservation.

Reported inline-reply frequencies describe different lists and collection periods; manual and automated counts also differ in measurement method. Their difference is not extractor recall or a business-email population estimate.

If several quotes and responses share a block, the Figure 6 property chain links each quote to each response. Whether all such links match intended reply scope needs testing; no scope error rate is reported.

proposed_experiments.proposal: On user-reviewed work-email examples, compare whole-message evidence with quote–response links and sentence/clause/span/EDU/hybrid candidates. Retain original spans and unresolved links.
proposed_experiments.evaluation: Score unit boundaries, quote–response link precision/recall, and decision-bearing evidence omission/broadening separately. Do not report query match counts as Topic accuracy.

proposed_experiments.proposal: Annotate gold Topics independently from quote blocks. Include multiple Topics per message, one span in several Topics, and separated spans belonging to one Topic.
proposed_experiments.evaluation: Report gold representational coverage separately from predicted span/membership performance. Separate within-message discontinuity from thread-level recurrence.

proposed_experiments.proposal: Test copied, nested, edited, multi-source, and multi-quote replies, plus conditional or partial +1 responses. Preserve provenance uncertainty instead of forcing author or Topic identity.
proposed_experiments.evaluation: Measure attribution accuracy and reply-scope precision/recall against reviewed gold; count lost conditions/evidence and broadened approval/action scopes. Keep related messages and near-duplicate quote copies together when splitting data.
